primary_sources.finding: modern recursive removal uses no-follow descriptor-relative traversal; partial removal does not supply a caller ownership journal
primary_sources.application: persist root ownership and collection intent separately; reobserve process identities before resuming any removal

primary_sources.finding: open-directory removal enumerates from the supplied handle, then removes the directory; its recursive default does not enforce our no-mount-crossing contract
primary_sources.application: reuse existing cap-std pinned-directory enumeration; constrain child opens and unlink relative to verified handles rather than adopt recursive removal unchanged

primary_sources.finding: resolution flags forbid escape, links and mount crossings; O_PATH/NOFOLLOW can reference a final symlink without following it
primary_sources.application: same flags for every descendant; unlink contained symlinks themselves, refuse bind mounts, and require kernel support

primary_sources.finding: per-tracee injection options copy global configuration and count syscall instances; delays need not fabricate syscall returns
primary_sources.application: warm installation, delay actual supervisor fsetxattr/renameat2/unlinkat, verify actual objects/process context, send authenticated pidfd SIGKILL and stop the exact owned observer before positive absence checks
